text: For this reason the woman ought to have authority on her head, because of the angels.
display_text: For this reason the woman ought to have authority on her head, because of the angels.
deferral_reason: The authority-on-her-head statement because of the angels has no sufficiently specific independently read parallel that explains that rationale. The text is preserved without supplying an unprinted word symbol, identifying the angels, or resolving the interpretation through a generic angel reference.

text: Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; those living in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
display_text: Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; those living in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
deferral_reason: The region list is read with the hearers native-language question and its next list segment. It does not identify individual speakers or support a later Church-founding route from recurring place names; no further specific pair is retained.

text: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene; visitors from Rome,
display_text: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene; visitors from Rome,
deferral_reason: The actual continuation includes Roman visitors and places as far as Libya around Cyrene. Those audience labels do not identify a later Roman correspondent or reproduce a mission journey. The list remains unpaired in this review.

text: On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing, sat on the tribunal, and delivered an address to them.
display_text: On an appointed day Herod put on royal clothing, sat on the tribunal, and delivered an address to them.
deferral_reason: The appointed-day royal address follows a peace petition and precedes the divine-voice acclamation. I retain no external comparison for this particular royal appearance; another tribunal or royal robe would not establish its audience or occasion.

text: After taking security from Jason and the others, the officials released them.
display_text: After taking security from Jason and the others, the officials released them.
deferral_reason: Security is taken from Jason and the others before release. The next night departure concerns Paul and Silas and supplies no second description of this legal security or its amount; these protective actions are not treated as the same procedure.

text: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners staying there spent their free time doing nothing but telling or hearing the latest thing.
display_text: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners staying there spent their free time doing nothing but telling or hearing the latest thing.
deferral_reason: The leisure notice explains the audience interest in strange teaching, not an explicit general condemnation of curiosity. I retain no moralizing comparison based on the latest-thing vocabulary alone.

text: So Paul went out from their midst.
display_text: So Paul went out from their midst.
deferral_reason: Paul leaves after mixed reactions to resurrection teaching. The next notice of some believers prevents turning this departure into rejection by everyone or an unstated expulsion; a generic departure is not retained as a parallel.

text: But some people joined him and believed, among them Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
display_text: But some people joined him and believed, among them Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
deferral_reason: The named believers and others are read in their particular Athenian setting. No actual second account of Dionysius or Damaris is established by the departure or next-city itinerary, and no later office or biography is supplied.

text: He left there and entered the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was next to the synagogue.
display_text: He left there and entered the house of a man named Titius Justus, a worshiper of God, whose house was next to the synagogue.
deferral_reason: The adjoining house belongs to Titius Justus, a worshiper of God. The following Crispus household belief notice names a different person; neither the juxtaposition nor a later similar name establishes a shared identity.

text: They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the tribunal. Gallio cared about none of these things.
display_text: They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the tribunal. Gallio cared about none of these things.
deferral_reason: The synagogue ruler Sosthenes is beaten and Gallio remains unconcerned. The already reviewed Corinthian greeting names a Sosthenes without narrating his conversion or giving an identity bridge; a same-name identification remains unretained.

text: There were about twelve men in all.
display_text: There were about twelve men in all.
deferral_reason: About twelve is explicitly approximate and the people are unnamed in this notice. Their Spirit reception and the following teaching do not identify them with the apostolic Twelve or substantiate another group by a number alone.

text: Completing the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the brothers, and stayed with them for one day.
display_text: Completing the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, greeted the brothers, and stayed with them for one day.
deferral_reason: The one-day Ptolemais visit is located after Tyre and before Caesarea. Other greetings and port stays would supply a common action rather than a precise second account of this itinerary, so it remains deferred.

text: Some disciples from Caesarea also went with us, taking us to a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
display_text: Some disciples from Caesarea also went with us, taking us to a certain Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
deferral_reason: The text names Mnason of Cyprus as an early disciple and proposed host. Neither the nearby Philip lodging nor the Jerusalem welcome identifies Mnason with another host or supplies an otherwise unstated history.

text: We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
display_text: We crossed the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia and came to Myra in Lycia.
deferral_reason: The original route crosses the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia to Myra in Lycia. The next Alexandrian ship change is a distinct action, and province overlaps alone do not establish another matching leg.

text: They took a sounding and found twenty fathoms. After going a little farther, they sounded again and found fifteen fathoms.
display_text: They took a sounding and found twenty fathoms. After going a little farther, they sounded again and found fifteen fathoms.
deferral_reason: Both actual soundings, twenty and fifteen fathoms, are preserved. Nearby suspected land and fear of rocks explain danger, but no retained counterpart duplicates these measurements or licenses an unstated distance or speed calculation.

text: We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.
display_text: We put in at Syracuse and stayed three days.
deferral_reason: The three days at Syracuse remain a specific stop between the island departure and Rhegium. Matching another three-day interval would only reproduce a number, without the same stop or a further specific relationship.

text: From there we cast off and reached Rhegium. After one day a south wind arose, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
display_text: From there we cast off and reached Rhegium. After one day a south wind arose, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.
deferral_reason: The route names Rhegium and Puteoli with a one-day interval and south wind. Another south-wind account would not establish these ports, elapsed time or an identical sailing occasion.

text: Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
display_text: Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
deferral_reason: The invitation is to the wedding already set in Cana; the surrounding mother and wine-shortage notices do not identify the hosts or explain who issued the invitation. No generic wedding comparison is retained.

text: ⟦And each went to his own house.
display_text: ⟦And each went to his own house.
deferral_reason: Each going home is kept within the original double-bracketed passage. Jesus going to the Mount of Olives is a distinct destination, not a basis for mapping every persons home or claiming independent attestation of the departure.

text: Jesus answered, “Do you say this from yourself, or did others tell you about Me?”
display_text: Jesus answered, “Do you say this from yourself, or did others tell you about Me?”
deferral_reason: The actual ensuing reply names Jesus nation and chief priests as the delivering party. It does not explicitly choose the from-yourself or others-told-you alternative; no unspoken source or motive for Pilates question is inserted.

text: of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
display_text: of Matthat, of Levi, of Melchi, of Jannai, of Joseph,
deferral_reason: Matthat, Levi, Melchi, Jannai and Joseph form the exact local sequence after Heli. Familiar names in a different generation would not establish the same chain; no identity or supplementary generation is inserted.

text: of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli, of Naggai,
display_text: of Mattathias, of Amos, of Nahum, of Esli, of Naggai,
deferral_reason: The actual Mattathias, Amos, Nahum, Esli and Naggai chain is read between its neighboring segments. Prophetic book-name similarities do not identify these ancestors with those writers.

text: of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Josech, of Joda,
display_text: of Maath, of Mattathias, of Semein, of Josech, of Joda,
deferral_reason: Maath, Mattathias, Semein, Josech and Joda retain their printed order before Joanan and Rhesa. No other succession has been established by similar names, so this ancestry segment remains unpaired.

text: of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
display_text: of Melchi, of Addi, of Cosam, of Elmadam, of Er,
deferral_reason: Melchi, Addi, Cosam, Elmadam and Er remain at their actual place after Neri. The adjacent ancestry does not justify mapping the segment onto unrelated same-name persons or a differently ordered genealogy.

text: of Jesus, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
display_text: of Jesus, of Eliezer, of Jorim, of Matthat, of Levi,
deferral_reason: Jesus, Eliezer, Jorim, Matthat and Levi are the stated ancestral names. The ancestor called Jesus is not identified with the Christ by his name alone, and repeated Matthat or Levi names do not collapse the generations.

text: of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam, of Eliakim,
display_text: of Simeon, of Judah, of Joseph, of Jonam, of Eliakim,
deferral_reason: Simeon, Judah, Joseph, Jonam and Eliakim lead into the following segment toward Nathan and David. Common patriarchal names do not furnish a securely matched second pedigree or license harmonized parentage.

text: And they spoke many other things against Him, blaspheming.
display_text: And they spoke many other things against Him, blaspheming.
deferral_reason: The narrator reports many other blasphemous sayings without their wording. The neighboring prophesy taunt does not supply the exact additional sayings, and the daybreak council remains a subsequent setting.

text: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people
display_text: Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people
deferral_reason: Pilate summons chief priests, rulers and people before announcing his examination. This notice does not identify every attendee or reproduce a different hearing; the shared ruler or crowd language is not retained as a precise external match.

text: Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud;
display_text: Azor begot Zadok; Zadok begot Achim; Achim begot Eliud;
deferral_reason: The actual Azor, Zadok, Achim and Eliud succession is retained between its neighboring generations. An isolated Zadok or other common name does not substantiate the whole ancestry segment or a second matching line.

text: Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
display_text: Eliud begot Eleazar; Eleazar begot Matthan; Matthan begot Jacob;
deferral_reason: Eliud, Eleazar, Matthan and Jacob form the printed sequence toward Joseph. Neighboring continuation and a separately named Eleazar do not establish a distinct parallel pedigree; no missing links are supplied.

text: But He did not answer her a word. His disciples came and asked Him, “Dismiss her, because she is crying out behind us.”
display_text: But He did not answer her a word. His disciples came and asked Him, “Dismiss her, because she is crying out behind us.”
deferral_reason: Jesus silence and the disciples dismissal request have different speakers from the ensuing lost-sheep reply. The text does not state an inner reason for the silence, and another supplicants experience is not equated with this one.

text: When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were exceedingly grieved. They came and explained to their master everything that had happened.
display_text: When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were exceedingly grieved. They came and explained to their master everything that had happened.
deferral_reason: The fellow slaves are grieved by the imprisonment and report what happened before the masters summons. No external reporting episode or every observers inner motive is established; I retain no separate comparison for the reporting notice in this review.

text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves!
display_text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel around sea and dry land to make one proselyte, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves!
deferral_reason: The accusation combines sea-and-land effort, one convert and the twice-as-much Gehenna outcome. Other mission or convert notices do not establish those stated particulars or justify generalizing the accusation to every mission.

text: Then all those virgins arose and put their lamps in order.
display_text: Then all those virgins arose and put their lamps in order.
deferral_reason: The virgins rise and arrange lamps in response to the midnight cry. I retain no merely verbal waking or lamp parallel and do not identify their equipment with sanctuary lamps.

text: On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
display_text: On the next day, which was after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
deferral_reason: The chief priests and Pharisees gather before Pilate on the day after Preparation. Earlier trial gatherings have different times and purposes; this notice alone does not support a matching summons or an imported calendar calculation.

text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
display_text: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
deferral_reason: Ampliatus is named as Pauls beloved in the Lord. This greeting supplies no second identified episode or task, and the broadly shared beloved formula alone remains insufficient for a retained specific pair.

text: Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.
display_text: Greet Apelles, approved in Christ. Greet those of Aristobulus’s household.
deferral_reason: Apelles is approved in Christ and members of Aristobulus household are greeted. The two descriptions remain distinct, with no household ownership, conversion history or identity with another named Christian supplied from a formula.

text: Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.
display_text: Greet Herodion my kinsman. Greet those of Narcissus’s household who are in the Lord.
deferral_reason: Herodion is called a kinsman; the greeted members of Narcissus household are those in the Lord. These labels do not establish a precise blood relationship, a Herod identity or Narcissus own belief.

text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
display_text: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
deferral_reason: Rufus and his mother and mine are the actual greeting. A repeated name elsewhere does not establish the same Rufus, and no biological adoption, maternal identity or unprinted kinship history is determined here.

text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
display_text: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.
deferral_reason: Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas and the brothers with them remain a particular greeting group. A common Hermes name or a generic greeting offers no secure matching person, event or task.

text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
display_text: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints with them.
deferral_reason: Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas and the saints with them are read as printed. No spouses, sisters personal name, meeting address or further identified episode is established by the greeting.
